newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - April 23.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on April 23:

LIMA - In a blaze of gunfire and explosions, Peruvian commandos stormed the hijacked Japanese embassy residence, killing the band of Marxist guerrillas who seized it 126 days ago and freeing most of the 72 hostages unharmed.

BUENOS AIRES - His plain white dress shirt was covered by a flak jacket and his only visible weapon was a walkie-talkie, but when President Alberto Fujimori walked triumphantly onto the grounds of the Japanese ambassador's residence he was every inch the conquering general.

GRAND FORKS, N.D. - President Clinton flew over the lake that was once a city, declaring he never had seen anything like it and promising an all-out federal effort to restore this flooded flatland region.

WASHINGTON - The Whitewater prosecutor won a six-month extension of a Little Rock grand jury, saying that the panel has heard "extensive evidence" of possible obstruction of justice and that he needs more time to complete his investigation.
WASHINGTON - A proposal to let Fairfax County schools stop offering band and orchestra lessons during the regular school day has sparked an intense debate over whether music instruction is a luxury.

WASHINGTON - The United States backed away from strictly enforcing the U.S.-patrolled "no-fly" zone over Iraq, allowing the Baghdad government to send civilian helicopters to pick up Iraqis returning from an Islamic pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia.
